newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Analysts see Kelgran bid for Kudu.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Kelgran bid for Kudu.

text.p: South African granite producer Kelgran Ltd is expected to launch an agreed bid for rival Kudu Granite after the two firms issued a cautionary announcement to shareholders on Tuesday, analysts said.
The move will be a further consolidation of the country's granite sector following Kelgran's acquisition of Ketter Granite Holdings in July.
Pretoria-based Kudu, which analysts say has a heavy debt burden, also held talks with Ketter earlier this year.
No executives at Kudu or Kelgran were immediately available for comment.
Analysts said a Kelgran bid for Kudu now looks almost certain. "It's been in the wind for the last two years and it looks like now it's about to happen," said one analyst.

Earlier today the two firms said in a joint statement that their controlling shareholders were in negotiations which might affect the two firms' share prices. The companies advised shareholders to be cautious when dealing in their shares until a further announcement was made.

Analysts said the two groups would fit well together. Kelgran's higher value product line would complement Kudu's more bulk-based commodity operations. "It's perfect. It's putting two very complementary things together," said one analyst.

Analysts were unsure of what any asking price for Kudu could be, but one of them estimated it at about 75 million rand. At 0850 GMT Kudu shares were up 12 cents to 152, while Kelgran nudged up five cents to 445.
Analysts and industry figures alike are convinced of a bright future for the granite sector, driven by growing construction demand.

In August, Henry Laas, Kelgran's managing director, predicted strong and growing demand for granite for the next two to three years. Earlier this month shares across the sector firmed on an optimistic outlook from Marlin Corp.
Kudu is 56 percent owned by Germany's Deutsche Steinindustrie and Kelgran is 57.4 percent controlled by Malaysia's Mycom SA, which bought the stake from Gencor Ltd in April.
